unit.title: Conduct research and prepare a marketing plan to achieve goals

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A Mandeville juice company aims to grow its profit by 10% next year. Which marketing objective supports that goal best?
options: Make the brand much better known across the whole island
Raise 1-litre sales in Manchester and St Elizabeth by 15% this year
Run more radio and social media advertisements than last year
Win an award for the new label design during the year

questions.stem: Why should the objectives in a marketing plan be drawn from the organisation's business plan?
options: So the marketing plan can be written more quickly by the team
So the marketing budget can be set higher than before
So the sales team no longer needs its own targets
So marketing work helps the firm reach its overall goals

questions.stem: Kemar Thompson must find out why sales of his firm's bottled water have fallen in Montego Bay. What should he do first?
options: Design a questionnaire for shoppers in the town
Hire an outside research agency straight away to run a survey
Write down the research problem and the questions to answer
Cut the price to win back the lost customers

questions.stem: Which is an example of secondary research for a marketing plan?
options: A focus group with eight young mothers in Spanish Town
Visitor arrival figures published by a public agency
A street survey of shoppers in Half Way Tree
Watching how customers move around the firm's shop

questions.stem: In which situation is primary research usually needed?
options: When the research budget is very small indeed
When the manager needs the results by tomorrow
When the facts needed do not yet exist anywhere
When published figures already answer the question

questions.stem: A Negril hotel wants to understand, in depth, how guests feel about its spa. Which method suits this best?
options: A large online survey made up of tick boxes
In-depth interviews with a small group of guests
A count of how many guests use the spa each week
A review of the spa's monthly sales figures

questions.stem: What is the main strength of quantitative research?
options: It explains the feelings behind each customer's choice
It needs no planning or careful choice of sample
It gives figures that can be measured and compared
It always costs less than any other method

questions.stem: A firm wants the views of its 4,000 account customers but has time to survey only 400. Which approach gives the fairest sample?
options: Ask the 400 customers who spend the most
Ask the first 400 customers who walk in
Ask staff to pick 400 friendly customers
Pick 400 at random from the full list

questions.stem: Which survey question is written best?
options: How many times did you buy from us last month?
Don't you agree that our prices are very fair?
How do you rate our prices and our delivery?
Do you use our app regularly and frequently?

questions.stem: Why should a questionnaire be pilot-tested before the main survey?
options: To collect enough answers to skip the main survey
To show senior managers that the work has started
To find unclear questions before the main survey
To make sure that respondents agree with the firm

questions.stem: A survey was emailed to 1,000 customers and 60 replied. What is the response rate?
Most replies to a customer survey came from people who had recently complained. What is the main risk?
options: The report will be too long for managers to read
The survey will cost more than the budget allowed
The firm will have too much data to analyse
The results may not represent all customers

questions.stem: Before interviewing a customer for research, what must the researcher do?
options: Promise the person a free gift for any answer
Record the interview secretly to get honest views
Tell the person which answers the firm hopes for
Explain the purpose and get the person's consent

questions.stem: Survey forms collect customers' names, phone numbers and opinions. In line with the data protection law, what should the firm do?
options: Sell the list to partners to recover research costs
Use the details only for the stated purpose, kept secure
Keep the forms in an open tray so staff can find them
Post the best comments online with customers' names

questions.stem: In a taste test, 72 of 120 people preferred the new recipe. What percentage is this?
Yearly sales of packaged plantain chips in Jamaica total J$800 million. One firm's sales are J$120 million. What is its market share?
Research shows that 40% of customers find the firm's website hard to use. What should the planner do with this finding?
options: Use it to set an objective and actions in the plan
Leave it out because it reflects badly on the firm
Repeat the survey until the figure comes out lower
Pass it to the IT team and leave it out of the plan

questions.stem: What is market segmentation?
options: Selling the same product in the same way to all
Dividing a market into groups with similar needs
Splitting the marketing budget equally across months
Sharing out the market with rivals by agreement

questions.stem: A Kingston gym groups possible members by their lifestyle, values and interests. Which kind of segmentation is this?
options: Psychographic
Geographic
Demographic
Behavioural

questions.stem: A bakery's research identifies three customer segments. Which is the most attractive one to target?
options: A growing segment it can serve better than rivals
The largest segment, already served well by two big rivals
A small segment that buys only once a year
A segment its delivery vans cannot reach

questions.stem: In a marketing plan, what does 'positioning' mean?
options: Where the product sits on the supermarket shelf
The order in which products appear in the price list
How customers see the brand compared with rivals
The firm's ranking in a national business award

questions.stem: Which information is most useful when analysing a rival for a marketing plan?
options: The number of years its owner has been in business
Its prices, target customers, strengths and weaknesses
The age and model of its office computers
The exact street address of its head office

questions.stem: A former employee of a rival offers a manager that rival's confidential price list. What should she do?
options: Use it, since the employee chose to share it
Copy it quickly and give back the original
Pay a small fee so that the exchange is fair
Refuse it and rely on lawful public sources

questions.stem: For services, the 7Ps add three elements to the original 4Ps. Which three?
options: Profit, planning and partnership
People, process and physical evidence
Packaging, publicity and persuasion
Policy, performance and premises

questions.stem: A courier service in May Pen is getting complaints about late and lost parcels. Which 'P' of the services mix needs attention first?
options: Process
Price
Promotion
Physical evidence

questions.stem: A new firm sets a low price to win many customers quickly, planning to raise it later. What is this strategy called?
options: Price skimming
Cost-plus pricing
Premium pricing
Penetration pricing

questions.stem: A product costs J$1,200 to make and the firm adds a 40% mark-up on cost. What is the selling price before GCT?
When a marketing plan sets prices for goods sold to the public, how should GCT be handled?
options: Ignored, because customers pay it to the government
Allowed for at the current rate when setting prices
Added only for customers who pay by card
Paid by the firm out of its marketing budget

questions.stem: A craft producer in Port Antonio wants to reach overseas buyers at low cost. Which channel suits best?
options: A new shop opened in a large city abroad
Door-to-door selling across the parish
Its own online shop with courier delivery
Selling only at the local Saturday market

questions.stem: Which promotion method best builds long-term trust with business buyers of office equipment?
options: Personal selling by trained account staff
A one-day half-price flash sale
Flyers placed on car windscreens
A radio jingle played late at night

questions.stem: A firm's social media posts get many likes but very few sales. What should the planner look at first?
options: Whether to post twice as often as now
Whether to close the social media accounts
Whether the posts reach and persuade target buyers
Whether staff are liking the posts themselves

questions.stem: A firm sets its marketing budget at 5% of expected sales of J$48,000,000. What is the budget?
Which way of setting the marketing budget links spending most closely to the plan's goals?
options: Spend whatever is left after all other costs
Match whatever the biggest rival spends
Keep last year's figure without any review
Cost the tasks needed to meet each goal

questions.stem: A campaign cost J$600,000 and brought in 240 new customers. What was the cost per new customer?
Which tool best shows the timing of each marketing activity across the year?
options: A Gantt chart
A pie chart
A SWOT grid
An organisation chart

questions.stem: Why should every action in a marketing plan have a named owner?
options: So the plan looks longer and more complete
So someone is accountable for getting it done
So the manager has less work to do
So that costs can be charged to the staff who did the work

questions.stem: The objective is 'win 300 new account customers by June'. Which key performance indicator (KPI) fits it best?
options: Number of posts placed on social media
Amount spent on printing brochures
New accounts opened each month
Number of staff in the sales team

questions.stem: Halfway through the year, sales are 20% behind the plan's target. What should the marketing manager do first?
options: Wait to see whether the second half is better
Lower the target so the plan looks met
Find out why, then adjust the actions
Double the advertising spend at once

questions.stem: The target was 500 enquiries and the actual figure is 425. What percentage of the target was achieved?
Which section should open a written marketing plan for senior managers?
options: A summary of goals, actions and budget
The full survey questionnaire
A list of every competitor's address
Detailed tables of raw survey data

questions.stem: In a PESTLE scan, rising fuel prices that push up delivery costs belong under which heading?
options: Political
Social
Technological
Economic

questions.stem: Sales of a firm's main product have levelled off and rivals are cutting prices. Which stage of the product life cycle is this?
options: Introduction
Growth
Maturity
Decline

questions.stem: An advertisement says a juice is '100% natural', but it contains added colouring. What is the main problem?
options: None, as long as sales rise after the advertisement
None, because many other firms make the same claim
It may mislead buyers, against consumer protection law
It matters only if a rival firm complains about it

questions.stem: Why should the marketing manager consult the sales and finance teams before finalising the plan?
options: To check that the plan is realistic and affordable
To share the blame with them if the plan later fails
To let them write the plan in her place
To delay the plan until the next year

questions.stem: Research shows young customers in Kingston learn about new products mainly through short videos on their phones. What should the plan do?
options: Keep using only newspaper advertisements
Stop selling to young customers altogether
Ignore it, because it comes from one survey
Move this segment's spend to short videos

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What one-word name is given to research that collects new data first-hand, for example by survey or interview?
What one-word name is given to research that uses data already collected by others, such as published statistics?
What is the smaller group of people chosen to represent the whole population in a survey called?
A survey went to 800 customers and 200 replied. What was the response rate, as a percentage?
What one-word term describes a survey question that pushes the respondent towards a particular answer?
What two-word term names the group of customers a marketing plan chooses to focus on?
What three-letter short form names a measurable value used to track progress towards a marketing goal?
What is the pricing strategy called in which a high launch price is charged to early buyers and lowered later?
A campaign cost J$300,000 and produced 1,500 enquiries. What was the cost per enquiry, in J$?
A firm's sales are J$90 million in a market worth J$450 million a year. What is its market share, as a percentage?
Which five-letter word sums up objectives that are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound?
Product, price, place and promotion together are called the marketing what? (One word.)
What is a small trial run of a questionnaire with a few people, before the main survey, called?
What two-word term names a small discussion group, led by a moderator, used to explore customers' views?
In the product life cycle, which stage follows maturity?

essays.stem: A juice maker in St Elizabeth plans to launch a reduced-sugar drink. Plan the market research it should carry out before writing the marketing plan, and justify your choice of methods.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would write a clear research brief: the problem (will enough people buy a reduced-sugar drink at a profitable price?), the questions to answer, the budget and the deadline. I would start with secondary research, because it is quick and cheap: health and population statistics, trade reports on soft-drink sales, and rivals' products, prices and shelf space in supermarkets. This shows the size and trend of the market. I would then fill the gaps with primary research. Two or three focus groups in different parishes would explore attitudes to sugar, taste and price in depth. A short survey of about 300 shoppers, chosen at random at several outlets, would give figures I can measure, such as the share who would buy and at what price. A blind taste test would compare our drink with the leading rivals. I would pilot the questionnaire first, get consent and keep the data secure under the data protection law. The mix of methods balances cost, depth and reliability, so the plan rests on evidence rather than opinion.
markingPoints: Writes a research brief: problem, questions, budget and deadline
Uses secondary research first and says why (cost, speed, market size and trend)
Uses suitable primary methods (focus groups, survey, taste test) to fill the gaps
Addresses sampling and pilot testing for reliable results
Includes consent and data protection, and justifies the mix of methods

essays.stem: Compare primary and secondary research for a marketing plan. Give the main advantages and limits of each, and recommend when a manager should use each one.
essays.modelAnswer: Secondary research uses information that already exists, such as government statistics, trade association reports, newspapers, rivals' websites and the firm's own sales records. Its advantages are speed and low cost, and it often covers the whole market over several years, which helps to show size and trends. Its limits are that it was collected for someone else's purpose, may be out of date, and rarely answers questions about our own customers or product. Primary research is collected first-hand for our purpose, through surveys, interviews, focus groups, observation or test sales. It is up to date, specific and confidential to the firm, so rivals do not have it. However, it costs more, takes longer and needs skill to design and sample properly, or it may be biased. I would recommend that a manager always starts with secondary research to understand the market and to sharpen the questions, then uses primary research only to fill the gaps that matter for the decision, such as customer needs, price sensitivity or reactions to a new product. This gets the best evidence for the money spent.
markingPoints: Defines secondary research with examples
Gives advantages and limits of secondary research
Defines primary research with examples
Gives advantages and limits of primary research
Recommends a sensible order or use: secondary first, primary to fill key gaps

essays.stem: Explain how a manager can make sure that survey findings are reliable enough to base a marketing plan on.
essays.modelAnswer: The manager must control quality at every stage. First, the sample must represent the target market. A random or carefully structured sample is better than asking whoever is easiest to reach, and it must be large enough for the decision being made. Second, the questionnaire must be well designed: one idea per question, clear everyday words, no leading or loaded questions, and answer choices that cover all options. A pilot test with a few people finds unclear questions before the main survey. Third, data collection must be consistent: interviewers are briefed to ask questions the same way and not to suggest answers, and the time and place of the survey avoid an unusual day. Fourth, the response rate and any non-response bias should be checked, for example if only unhappy customers replied. Fifth, data entry and analysis should be checked twice, and findings compared with other sources such as sales records or published data. Finally, the report should state the sample size, method and limits honestly, so senior managers know how much weight the findings can bear.
markingPoints: Representative sample of a suitable size
Sound questionnaire design and a pilot test
Consistent, unbiased data collection
Checks response rate, bias and accuracy of analysis; compares with other sources
Reports the method and limits honestly

essays.stem: Describe how a hotel in Montego Bay could segment its market, choose target segments and position a new day-pass offer for local residents.
essays.modelAnswer: Segmentation means dividing the local market into groups with similar needs. The hotel could segment residents by geography (Montego Bay and nearby parishes), by demographics (young professionals, families with children, retired couples), by lifestyle (people who value relaxation, fitness or social events) and by behaviour (people who already eat out or buy staycations). Research such as a short survey and a review of past local bookings would show the size, spending power and needs of each group. Targeting means choosing the segments that are large or growing, profitable, reachable and a good fit with the hotel's facilities. For example, families at weekends and young professionals on public holidays may be the best targets, while groups the hotel cannot serve well are left out. Positioning means deciding how the hotel wants these customers to see the day pass compared with beaches, clubs and other hotels. It might be positioned as 'an affordable luxury day out, close to home', supported by a clear price in J$, a family package with lunch, and photos showing safe pools and friendly staff.
markingPoints: Explains segmentation and gives sensible bases (geographic, demographic, lifestyle, behaviour)
Uses research to size and understand segments
Explains targeting criteria and chooses realistic target segments
Explains positioning against alternatives
Supports the position with a consistent offer (price, package, message)

essays.stem: Using the 7Ps, recommend a marketing mix for a new mobile car-wash service in Portmore, and justify each part.
essays.modelAnswer: Product: a basic wash, a full valet and a monthly plan, using water-saving equipment and safe products, because busy commuters want convenience and choice. Price: clear J$ prices for each service, with GCT allowed for at the current rate, a lower monthly plan price to build repeat business, and prices checked against car-wash rivals. Place: the service comes to the customer at home or at work in Portmore, booked by phone, website or messaging app, because convenience is the main benefit. Promotion: social media posts and short videos showing before-and-after results, flyers in housing schemes, and a referral discount, aimed at working adults with cars. People: trained, polite, uniformed staff, because customers let them handle their cars and must trust them. Process: easy online booking, text reminders, arrival within a set time window and quick payment by card or mobile, so the experience is smooth. Physical evidence: branded vans, clean uniforms, a checklist left with the customer and online reviews, which show quality before people buy. Together these parts give one clear message: reliable, convenient care for your car.
markingPoints: Product and price set out with reasons (including GCT at the current rate)
Place and promotion suited to the target customers
People: trained, trustworthy staff
Process and physical evidence that support service quality
Parts fit together into one consistent offer

essays.stem: Explain why marketing objectives must be SMART and linked to the organisation's goals. Rewrite the objective 'increase sales a lot' as a SMART objective and justify your version.
essays.modelAnswer: Marketing objectives guide every later decision in the plan: the target segments, the mix, the budget and the measures. If they are vague, staff cannot tell what success looks like, spending cannot be judged, and progress cannot be checked. SMART objectives are specific about what will change, measurable with a figure, achievable with the resources available, relevant to the business goals, and time-bound with a deadline. Linking them to the organisation's goals makes sure that marketing helps the business as a whole, for example by growing profitable sales rather than simply winning attention. 'Increase sales a lot' fails every test. A better version is: 'Increase sales of our 500 ml juice range to supermarkets in Kingston and St Andrew from J$20 million to J$23 million, a rise of 15%, between January and December next year.' It is specific (one range, one channel, one area), measurable (J$ figures), achievable if research shows the market is growing and the sales team has capacity, relevant because the business plan aims to grow profit from its core range, and time-bound by the end of December.
markingPoints: Explains why clear objectives matter for planning, spending and measuring
Explains each SMART element
Explains the link to organisational goals
Rewrites the objective in a SMART form with correct figures (J$20m to J$23m is 15%)
Justifies each element of the rewritten objective

essays.stem: A firm has J$3,000,000 for marketing next year. Explain how you would allocate and justify this budget across activities, and how you would control the spending.
essays.modelAnswer: I would use the objective-and-task method: cost the activities needed to reach each objective, then check the total against the J$3,000,000 available. If research shows that our target customers are mostly online, a sensible split is: digital advertising and content J$1,200,000 (40%); in-store sampling and events J$750,000 (25%); radio J$600,000 (20%); printed and point-of-sale material J$300,000 (10%); and a contingency of J$150,000 (5%). These add up to J$3,000,000 and 100%. Each line is justified by the objective it serves and the audience it reaches; for example, sampling supports trial of a new product, and radio reaches older rural buyers. The budget would be phased by month to match the campaign calendar and the seasons when customers buy. To control it, each line has a named budget holder, spending needs approval against the line, and actual spending is compared with the budget every month. I would also track results, such as cost per lead and sales per campaign, so money can be moved from activities that do not work to those that do.
markingPoints: Uses a sound method such as objective-and-task
Gives a realistic allocation that adds up to J$3,000,000 (and 100%)
Justifies each line by objective and audience; includes a contingency
Phases the budget over the year
Controls spending: budget holders, approvals, monthly comparison, results tracking

essays.stem: Describe how you would monitor a marketing plan during the year and evaluate its success at the end.
essays.modelAnswer: Monitoring starts in the plan itself. Each objective needs key performance indicators (KPIs) with targets and dates, such as monthly sales by product and area, number of new customers, website visits and enquiries, conversion rate, cost per new customer and customer satisfaction scores. Each action also has an owner, a deadline and a budget line. During the year I would collect the figures from sales records, the website, social media reports and short customer surveys, and put them in a simple dashboard. Each month the marketing team would compare actual results with targets and spending with budget, find the reasons for any gaps and agree corrective actions, such as changing a message, moving spend to a stronger channel or retraining staff. A short report would go to senior managers. At the end of the year, I would evaluate the plan as a whole: which objectives were met, what each activity cost compared with the results it produced, what customers and staff said, and what changed in the market. The lessons learned would feed directly into the next year's research and plan.
markingPoints: KPIs with targets and dates linked to the objectives
Sources of data and a dashboard or regular report
Regular comparison of actual with plan and budget, with corrective action
End-of-year evaluation of results against objectives and cost
Lessons learned fed into the next plan

essays.stem: Explain the main legal and ethical points a manager must consider when carrying out market research and putting a marketing plan into action in Jamaica.
essays.modelAnswer: In research, people must take part freely and know what the research is for. The researcher should get their consent, let them stop at any time, and take extra care with children, who need a parent's consent. Personal data such as names, phone numbers and opinions must be collected only for a stated purpose, kept secure, used only for that purpose and not kept longer than needed, in line with the data protection law. Results should be reported honestly, including their limits, rather than shaped to please managers. Information about rivals must come from lawful, public sources, not from stolen or confidential documents. In the marketing plan itself, advertising must be truthful: claims about price, health, quality or origin must be accurate and supported, because consumer protection law forbids misleading customers. Prices should be clear, with GCT handled at the current rate. The firm must not copy another firm's name, logo or designs, which intellectual property law protects. Marketing emails and messages should go only to people who have agreed to receive them, with an easy way to opt out.
markingPoints: Consent, voluntary participation and care with children in research
Data protection: purpose, security, limited use and storage
Honest reporting and lawful competitor information
Truthful advertising and clear pricing under consumer protection law
Respect for intellectual property and consent for direct marketing

essays.stem: Research shows that a large regional chain will open three stores next year in the towns where your firm sells household goods. Evaluate how your marketing plan should respond, and recommend a course of action.
essays.modelAnswer: First the plan must analyse the threat with evidence: the chain's likely prices, range, store locations, opening dates and target customers, and which of our customers and products are most at risk. A SWOT analysis would show where we are stronger, such as local knowledge, credit for regular customers, delivery and personal service, and where we are weaker, such as buying power and price. Competing head-on on price would probably fail, because the chain buys in bulk and can accept lower margins for longer. Doing nothing is also risky, because loyal customers may still try the new stores. A better response is to defend and differentiate. I would recommend that the plan focuses on our most loyal and profitable segments, strengthens the services the chain cannot easily copy (free delivery, credit accounts, fast service, local products), and launches a loyalty scheme before the chain opens. Price only on the items customers compare most. Set KPIs for customer retention and sales by store, and review them monthly after the chain opens so the plan can be adjusted quickly.
markingPoints: Analyses the competitor and the risk using evidence
Uses SWOT or similar to identify the firm's strengths and weaknesses
Evaluates options such as price war, doing nothing and differentiation
Recommends a justified strategy focused on strengths and loyal segments
Sets KPIs and monitoring to adjust the plan

practical1.title: Plan, run and analyse a small market research project
practical1.brief: The assessor gives your group a short case: a made-up Jamaican firm planning a new product or service (for example a healthy lunch box delivery service for office workers in New Kingston). As a group, plan and carry out a small research project to support its marketing plan. Give each member a named role: research lead (writes the research brief: problem, questions, methods, sample, timeline), questionnaire designer (writes a questionnaire of 8 to 12 questions and runs a pilot test with two people from another group), secondary researcher (finds and summarises at least three relevant secondary sources), data analyst (enters at least 20 anonymous responses from other trainees into a spreadsheet and makes charts, checking every figure twice), and report writer (writes a one-page findings summary with recommendations). In a group of four, the research lead also writes the summary. Every member collects some of the responses. Photograph each stage and hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Computers with internet access, spreadsheet and word processor software
Consent statement to read to each respondent
photos: The questionnaire before and after the pilot test, with changes marked
The spreadsheet of responses and the charts on screen
The one-page findings summary with recommendations
checklist: Took a named role and completed their part of the research
Research brief states a clear problem, questions, methods and sample
Questionnaire has clear, unbiased questions and was changed after the pilot
Collected responses politely, read the consent statement and kept answers anonymous
Figures, percentages and charts are correct and were checked twice
Findings summary draws sound conclusions and states the limits of the research
safety: Collect no names, phone numbers or other personal data; keep responses anonymous and secure
Respondents take part only if they agree, and may stop at any time
Treat respondents and group members with respect; disagree with ideas, not people
Share the workload fairly and take a short break

practical2.title: Prepare and present a one-year marketing plan
practical2.brief: Using your findings from Practical 1, or a research pack from the assessor, prepare a one-year marketing plan for the firm and present it to a management panel (the assessor and members of another group). The plan must contain: an executive summary; a short situation analysis (SWOT and PESTLE); three SMART marketing objectives linked to the firm's goals; target segments and a positioning statement; the marketing mix (7Ps); a budget in J$ that adds up to the amount the assessor gives, with a contingency; a Gantt chart of activities with owners; and KPIs for monitoring. Give each member a named role: plan leader (executive summary and objectives), market analyst (situation analysis, segments and positioning), mix designer (7Ps), finance lead (budget, checked twice), and monitoring lead (Gantt chart and KPIs). In a group of four, the plan leader also prepares the Gantt chart. Every member presents their part in a 10-minute presentation and answers at least one question from the panel. Photograph each stage and hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Findings from Practical 1 or a research pack from the assessor
Budget figure and firm's business goals from the assessor
Computers with spreadsheet, word processor and presentation software
photos: The SMART objectives with segments and positioning statement
The marketing budget spreadsheet on screen
The Gantt chart with owners and the KPI table
The group presenting to the panel
checklist: Took a named role and produced their section of the plan
Objectives are SMART and clearly linked to the firm's goals and the research
Segments, positioning and 7Ps fit together and suit the target customers
Budget adds up to the given amount, includes a contingency and was checked twice
Gantt chart and KPIs show who does what, when, and how success is measured
Presented clearly and answered a panel question with evidence
safety: Use only the made-up firm and the figures given; no real firm's confidential information
Use only anonymous research data in slides and reports
Respect the panel and other groups during questions
Keep projector cables out of walkways and share the workload fairly
